1.q: twenty-five thousand cubits in length … ten thousand cubits in width
1.note: Each cubit was about 54 centimeters. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 40:5. Alternate translation: [25,000 cubits long … 10,000 cubits wide] or [about 13.5 kilometers long … about 5.4 kilometers wide]
Alternate translation: [all of the area inside of the borders around it]

The number **10,000** is a translation of the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today. This reading, however, does not seem to make sense because verse 3 describes a portion of that same width that must fit within the portion described here. The Hebrew scribe may have used the number from verse 3 here by mistake. You may want to follow an alternative reading from the ancient Greek translation as the UST does, or you may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [20,000]

2.q: five hundred cubits … fifty cubits in width
2.note: Each cubit was about 54 centimeters. Alternate translation: [500 cubits … 50 cubits wide] or [about 270 meters … about 27 meters wide]

3.note: the temple and the border surrounding it
Each long cubit was about 54 centimeters. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 40:5. Alternate translation: [25,000 cubits … 10,000 cubits] or [about 13.5 kilometers … about 5.4 kilometers]

5.note: The phrase **20 chambers** is a translation of the standard written Hebrew text as we have it today. This reading, however, does not seem to make sense. With the UST, you may want to follow an alternative reading from the ancient Greek translation, which seems to have translated similar-looking Hebrew words, or you may want to follow the major translation in your area. Alternate translation: [towns to live in]

6.note: Each long cubit was about 54 centimeters. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 40:5. Alternate translation: [5,000 cubits … 25,000 cubits] or [about 2.7 kilometers … about 13.5 kilometers]
This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: [that you gave for the holy place]

7.q: The length will correspond to the length of one of those portions
7.note: It is implied that Ezekiel is comparing the prince’s land with the size of the land given to each of the tribes. Alternate translation: [The length will be the same as the length of one of the portions given to the tribes]

7.q: from the west to the east
7.note: It is implied that these are the western and eastern borders of the land of Israel. “from the western border of Israel at the sea to the eastern border at the Jordan River”

8.q: This land will be property for the prince in Israel
8.note: Alternate translation: [This portion of the land will be the property of the prince among the people of Israel]

9.q: this is the Lord Yahweh’s declaration
9.note: Yahweh speaks of himself by name to express the certainty of what he is declaring. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 5:11. Alternate translation: [this is what the Lord Yahweh has declared] or [this is what I, the Lord Yahweh, have declared]
Alternate translation: [You have done too many bad things] or [You have been acting badly for far too long]

10.note: an instrument that was used to weigh things that people sold or bought

11.q: so that a bath will be a tenth of a homer
11.note: Alternate translation: [so that ten baths will be the same amount as a homer]

13.note: It is implied that this is the amount of wheat that the people harvest. Alternate translation: [for every homer of wheat from the harvest]

14.q: The regulation offering of oil will be a tenth of a bath
14.note: Alternate translation: [You must offer one tenth of a bath of oil]

15.note: Alternate translation: [the parts of Israel that get a good amount of water]
This can be translated in active form. Alternate translation: [you will use for]

17.note: the festivals that happen at the same time every year or month or week

The word “house” is a metonym for the family that lives in the house, in this case the Israelites, the descendants of Jacob over many years. See how you translated this in [Ezekiel 3:1](ta:03). Alternate translation: [the Israelites] or [the Israelite people group]

18.note: Yahweh speaks of himself by name to remind Ezekiel and the people that what he is saying is important. See how you translated this in Ezekiel 6:11. Alternate translation: [I, the Lord Yahweh, say this]

18.q: In the first month, on the first day of the month
18.note: This is the first month of the Hebrew calendar. The first day is near the end of March on Western calendars. (See also: [Ordinal Numbers](ta:translate-ordinal))
The word “you” is singular and refers to whoever is the prince in Israel.

20.q: on the seventh of the month
20.note: “on the seventh day of the first month”

20.q: for each person’s sin by accident or ignorance
20.note: Alternate translation: [for each person who had sinned without meaning to or because he did not know he was sinning] or [for each person who had sinned by accident or because he did not now what was right]

21.q: In the first month on the fourteenth day of the month
21.note: This is the first month of the Hebrew calendar. The fourteenth day is near the beginning of April. (See also: [Ordinal Numbers](ta:translate-ordinal))
The word “you” is plural and refers to the prince and the rest of the people of the house of Israel.

23.q: Seven bulls and seven unblemished rams
23.note: Alternate translation: [Seven bulls and seven rams that are completely healthy]

24.note: This is also called a “grain offering.”
You may convert this to a modern measure. Alternate translation: [twenty-two liters]
You may convert this to a modern measure. Alternate translation: [four liters]
You may convert this to a modern measure. Alternate translation: [each twenty-two liters]

25.q: In the seventh month on the fifteenth day of the month
25.note: This is the seventh month of the Hebrew calendar. The fifteenth day is near the beginning of October. (See also: [Ordinal Numbers](ta:translate-ordinal))
This is a different festival from the festival Ezekiel was describing before.
